agent_id.description:
The ID to use for the agent, which will become the final component of
the agent's resource name. If not provided, a unique ID will be
automatically assigned for the agent.
agent_id.rationale: Specifies the unique identifier of the agent. This value is only used to identify the resource and does not control authentication, permissions, or data protection. Restricting the agent ID would not provide any meaningful security benefit.

app.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
app.rationale: Identifies the parent application that owns the agent. This is a resource reference, and platform security policies should not restrict which application a team uses. Restricting this field would be overreaching.

child_agents.description:
List of child agents in the agent tree.
Format: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/apps/{app}/agents/{agent}'
child_agents.rationale: References child agents that belong to the current agent. This field only links existing resources and does not directly affect the security configuration of the agent. Therefore, it is not a suitable policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls how Terraform handles resource deletion. A security policy can require a protective deletion setting to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorized deletion. This helps protect important resources from being removed unintentionally.

description.rationale: Provides a human-readable description of the agent. It is only used for documentation and does not affect authentication, access control, or data protection. Restricting this field would not improve security.

display_name.rationale: Specifies the display name shown for the agent. This field is only used for identification and does not control how the resource behaves or who can access it. Therefore, it is not a security policy target.

guardrails.description:
List of guardrails for the agent.
Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/apps/{app}/guardrails/{guardrail}'
guardrails.rationale: Specifies the guardrails applied to the agent. Guardrails help control the behaviour of the AI system and reduce unsafe responses. A policy can require guardrails to be configured to improve the overall security and safety of the agent.

instruction.description: Instructions for the LLM model to guide the agent's behavior.
instruction.rationale: Defines the instructions that guide the behaviour of the language model. Well-defined instructions help reduce unsafe or unintended behaviour. A security policy can require this field to be configured to encourage secure and responsible AI behaviour.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project where the resource is created. This is a resource reference, and platform policies should not enforce specific project IDs because different teams use different projects.

tools.description:
List of available tools for the agent.
Format: 'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/apps/{app}/tools/{tool}'
tools.rationale: References the tools available to the agent. It only points to existing resources and does not directly improve the security of the agent. Restricting tool references would be overreaching.

after_agent_callbacks.description:
The callbacks to execute after the agent is called.
The provided callbacks are executed sequentially in the exact order they
are given in the list. If a callback returns an overridden response,
execution stops and any remaining callbacks are skipped.

after_agent_callbacks.description.rationale: Provides a description for the callback. This field is only for documentation and does not influence the execution or security of the callback. Therefore, it is not a security policy target.

after_agent_callbacks.disabled.description:
Whether the callback is disabled. Disabled callbacks are ignored by the
agent.
after_agent_callbacks.disabled.rationale: Controls whether the post-turn callback executes. Callbacks are the resource's only mechanism for attaching guardrail/audit logic to the execution path. f it's set to true, the callback never runs. A policy should keep it enabled by default so teams don't accidentally turn off checks without realizing it.

after_agent_callbacks.python_code.description: The python code to execute for the callback.
after_agent_callbacks.python_code.rationale: Contains free-form execuitable Python code which is executed after the agent runs. A generic platform policy cannot reliably inspect or validate arbitrary Python scripts, so this field is not suitable for infrastructure policy enforcement. Security review of the code should be handled through application development and code review processes rather than platform policy.

after_model_callbacks.description:
The callbacks to execute after the model is called. If there are multiple
calls to the model, the callback will be executed multiple times.
The provided callbacks are executed sequentially in the exact order they
are given in the list. If a callback returns an overridden response,
execution stops and any remaining callbacks are skipped.

after_model_callbacks.description.rationale: Provides a description for the callback. It is only used for documentation and has no effect on the security of the resource.

after_model_callbacks.disabled.description:
Whether the callback is disabled. Disabled callbacks are ignored by the
agent.
after_model_callbacks.disabled.rationale: Controls whether the post-model-call callback executes. Since it could be doing checks on the model's output, it could be required to stays on unless there's a reason to turn it off. A security policy can check that.

after_model_callbacks.python_code.description: The python code to execute for the callback.
after_model_callbacks.python_code.rationale: Specifies free-form executable Python code that runs after model execution. A generic platform policy cannot reliably inspect or validate arbitrary Python scripts, so this field is not suitable for infrastructure policy enforcement. Security review of the code should be handled through application development and code review processes rather than platform policy.

after_tool_callbacks.description:
The callbacks to execute after the tool is invoked. If there are multiple
tool invocations, the callback will be executed multiple times.
The provided callbacks are executed sequentially in the exact order they
are given in the list. If a callback returns an overridden response,
execution stops and any remaining callbacks are skipped.

after_tool_callbacks.description.rationale: Provides a description of the callback. It does not affect execution or security and is only used for documentation purposes.

after_tool_callbacks.disabled.description:
Whether the callback is disabled. Disabled callbacks are ignored by the
agent.
after_tool_callbacks.disabled.rationale: Controls whether the post-tool callback executes. Tool calls are risky because they can do real actions. So, the callback that checks what happened after a tool runs should stay on by default instead of being turned off. A policy can check that.

after_tool_callbacks.python_code.description: The python code to execute for the callback.
after_tool_callbacks.python_code.rationale: Contains free-form executable Python code that runs after tool execution. A generic platform policy cannot reliably inspect or validate arbitrary Python scripts, so this field is not suitable for infrastructure policy enforcement. Security review of the code should be handled through application development and code review processes rather than platform policy.

before_agent_callbacks.description:
The callbacks to execute before the agent is called.
The provided callbacks are executed sequentially in the exact order they
are given in the list. If a callback returns an overridden response,
execution stops and any remaining callbacks are skipped.

before_agent_callbacks.description.rationale: Provides a description of the callback. It has no impact on the security or operation of the resource.

before_agent_callbacks.disabled.description:
Whether the callback is disabled. Disabled callbacks are ignored by the
agent.
before_agent_callbacks.disabled.rationale: Controls whether the callback executes before the agent runs. Disabling important validation callbacks may weaken security. So it should default to on so nothing gets silently skipped. A policy can check that.

before_agent_callbacks.python_code.description: The python code to execute for the callback.
before_agent_callbacks.python_code.rationale: Contains free-form executable Python code that runs before the agent executes. A generic platform policy cannot reliably inspect or validate arbitrary Python scripts, so this field is not suitable for infrastructure policy enforcement. Security review of the code should be handled through application development and code review processes rather than platform policy.

before_model_callbacks.description:
The callbacks to execute before the model is called. If there are multiple
calls to the model, the callback will be executed multiple times.
The provided callbacks are executed sequentially in the exact order they
are given in the list. If a callback returns an overridden response,
execution stops and any remaining callbacks are skipped.

before_model_callbacks.description.rationale: Used only to describe the callback. It does not affect security or resource behaviour.

before_model_callbacks.disabled.description:
Whether the callback is disabled. Disabled callbacks are ignored by the
agent.
before_model_callbacks.disabled.rationale: Determines whether the callback is enabled. Keeping important validation callbacks enabled helps maintain consistent security checks before model execution.

before_model_callbacks.python_code.description: The python code to execute for the callback.
before_model_callbacks.python_code.rationale: Contains free-from executable Python code executed before the model runs. A generic platform policy cannot reliably inspect or validate arbitrary Python scripts, so this field is not suitable for infrastructure policy enforcement. Security review of the code should be handled through application development and code review processes rather than platform policy.

before_tool_callbacks.description:
The callbacks to execute before the tool is invoked. If there are multiple
tool invocations, the callback will be executed multiple times.
The provided callbacks are executed sequentially in the exact order they
are given in the list. If a callback returns an overridden response,
execution stops and any remaining callbacks are skipped.

before_tool_callbacks.description.rationale: Provides documentation for the callback. It has no effect on the security configuration of the resource.

before_tool_callbacks.disabled.description:
Whether the callback is disabled. Disabled callbacks are ignored by the
agent.
before_tool_callbacks.disabled.rationale: Controls whether the callback is active. A policy can require important security callbacks to remain enabled to maintain protection.

before_tool_callbacks.python_code.description: The python code to execute for the callback.
before_tool_callbacks.python_code.rationale: Contains free-form executable Python code that runs before tool execution. A generic platform policy cannot reliably inspect or validate arbitrary Python scripts, so this field is not suitable for infrastructure policy enforcement. Security review of the code should be handled through application development and code review processes rather than platform policy.

llm_agent.description:
Default agent type. The agent uses instructions and callbacks specified in
the agent to perform the task using a large language model.

model_settings.description: Model settings contains various configurations for the LLM model.

model_settings.model.description:
The LLM model that the agent should use.
If not set, the agent will inherit the model from its parent agent.
model_settings.model.rationale: Specifies which language model the agent uses. Choosing a model is a functional configuration decision and does not directly represent a platform security control.

model_settings.temperature.description:
If set, this temperature will be used for the LLM model. Temperature
controls the randomness of the model's responses. Lower temperatures
produce responses that are more predictable. Higher temperatures produce
responses that are more creative.
model_settings.temperature.rationale: Controls the creativity and randomness of model responses. This affects application behaviour but does not directly improve infrastructure or platform security.

remote_dialogflow_agent.description:
The agent which will transfer execution to an existing remote
[Dialogflow](https://cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/concept/console-conversational-agents)
agent flow. The corresponding Dialogflow agent will process subsequent user
queries until the session ends or flow ends and the control is transferred
back to the parent CES agent.

remote_dialogflow_agent.agent.rationale: References an existing Dialogflow agent. It is only a resource reference and platform security policies should not restrict which agent is selected.

remote_dialogflow_agent.environment_id.description:
The environment ID of the Dialogflow agent be used for the agent
execution. If not specified, the draft environment will be used.
remote_dialogflow_agent.environment_id.rationale: Identifies the Dialogflow environment used during execution. This is a configuration reference and does not directly improve security.

remote_dialogflow_agent.flow_id.description: The flow ID of the flow in the Dialogflow agent.
remote_dialogflow_agent.flow_id.rationale: Identifies the Dialogflow flow to execute. Restricting flow identifiers would not improve the security of the resource.

remote_dialogflow_agent.input_variable_m.description:
The mapping of the app variables names to the Dialogflow session
parameters names to be sent to the Dialogflow agent as input.
remote_dialogflow_agent.input_variable_m.rationale: Maps application variables to Dialogflow parameters. This controls data mapping rather than security, so it is not an appropriate security policy target.

remote_dialogflow_agent.output_variable_.description:
The mapping of the Dialogflow session parameters names to the app
variables names to be sent back to the CES agent after the Dialogflow
agent execution ends.
remote_dialogflow_agent.output_variable_.rationale: Maps Dialogflow output values back to application variables. This is functional configuration and does not directly improve resource security.

remote_dialogflow_agent.respect_response.description: Indicates whether to respect the message-level interruption settings configured in the Dialogflow agent. * If false: all response messages from the Dialogflow agent follow the app-level barge-in settings. * If true: only response messages with ['allow_playback_interruption'](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dialogflow/cx/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.dialogflow.cx.v3#text) set to true will be interruptable, all other messages follow the app-level barge-in settings.
remote_dialogflow_agent.respect_response.rationale: Controls how response interruptions are handled during conversations. It affects user experience and conversation behaviour rather than platform security.

toolsets.description: List of toolsets for the agent.

toolsets.tool_ids.description: The tools IDs to filter the toolset.
toolsets.tool_ids.rationale: References specific tools within a toolset. It only identifies existing resources and does not directly improve the security of the agent.

toolsets.toolset.description:
The resource name of the toolset.
Format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/apps/{app}/toolsets/{toolset}'
toolsets.toolset.rationale: References the toolset used by the agent. This is a resource reference and should remain a team-specific configuration rather than a platform security policy.
